levels.title: Operating a service with pico-actuator
levels.description: Health probes, build info and metrics over HTTP: what an operator needs from a running service.

levels.title: Switching the actuator on
levels.description:
Endpoints you did not write

pico-actuator mounts a set of operational endpoints under /actuator on the same app pico-fastapi builds: health, info, metrics and refresh. It is auto-discovered like any pico module, so there is nothing to import; ActuatorSettings only decides whether the endpoints get mounted.

The labs drive it through FastAPI's TestClient, which runs the app in-process: the same requests a load balancer or a curl would send.

files.name: controllers.py
main.py
files.content:
from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from pico_boot import init
from pico_ioc import DictSource, configuration
import controllers

container = init(
    modules=[controllers],
    config=configuration(DictSource({
        "fastapi": {"title": "orders", "version": "1.0.0"},
        # This deployment shipped with the probes switched off, so the platform
        # has no way to tell whether the service is alive.
        # TODO: turn them back on.
        "actuator": {"enabled": False},
    })),
)

client = TestClient(container.get(FastAPI))
health = client.get("/actuator/health")

print(health.status_code, health.json())
assert health.status_code == 200, f"no health endpoint: {health.status_code}"
assert health.json()["status"] == "UP"
print("the service can now say whether it is alive")

solution.main.py:
from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from pico_boot import init
from pico_ioc import DictSource, configuration
import controllers

container = init(
    modules=[controllers],
    config=configuration(DictSource({
        "fastapi": {"title": "orders", "version": "1.0.0"},
        "actuator": {"enabled": True},
    })),
)

client = TestClient(container.get(FastAPI))
health = client.get("/actuator/health")

print(health.status_code, health.json())
assert health.status_code == 200, f"no health endpoint: {health.status_code}"
assert health.json()["status"] == "UP"
print("the service can now say whether it is alive")

hints: ActuatorSettings binds the actuator prefix of the configuration.
Its first field decides whether the endpoints get mounted at all.
"actuator": {"enabled": True} next to the fastapi block.

levels.title: Health that means something
levels.description:
Liveness is not readiness

A process that answers HTTP is not necessarily able to do its job. A HealthIndicator component contributes to /actuator/health: implement check() and return either a bool or a dict with a status key plus whatever detail helps whoever is paged.

If any indicator reports DOWN the endpoint answers 503, which is what makes a load balancer take the instance out of rotation before it starts failing requests.

files.name: app.py
main.py
files.content:
from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from pico_boot import init
from pico_ioc import DictSource, configuration
import app

container = init(
    modules=[app],
    config=configuration(DictSource({
        "fastapi": {"title": "orders", "version": "1.0.0"},
        "actuator": {"enabled": True},
    })),
)

client = TestClient(container.get(FastAPI))
print("empty queue :", client.get("/actuator/health").json())

container.get(app.OrderQueue).depth = 42
saturated = client.get("/actuator/health")
print("42 pending  :", saturated.status_code, saturated.json())

assert saturated.status_code == 503, f"expected 503, got {saturated.status_code}"
assert saturated.json()["components"]["QueueHealth"]["depth"] == 42
print("health follows business state, not just process liveness")

hints: HealthIndicator is imported already; the class has to be one.
The method is check(), and it may return a dict with a status key.

levels.title: Telling the world what is deployed
levels.description:
/actuator/info

An InfoContributor adds a fragment to the info document: implement contribute() and return a dict. Every contributor registered in the container is merged, so build metadata, feature flags and the config the service actually booted with can each come from their own component.

In a real deployment this is what tells you, from outside, which commit is running - the question you ask first when something behaves unexpectedly.

files.name: app.py
files.content:
from pico_ioc import component
from pico_actuator import InfoContributor


# TODO: expose the build metadata below at /actuator/info, so an operator can
# tell which commit is deployed without shelling into the container.
@component
class BuildInfo:
    COMMIT = "9f2c1ab"

files.name: main.py
files.content:
from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from pico_boot import init
from pico_ioc import DictSource, configuration
import app

container = init(
    modules=[app],
    config=configuration(DictSource({
        "fastapi": {"title": "orders", "version": "1.0.0"},
        "actuator": {"enabled": True},
    })),
)

client = TestClient(container.get(FastAPI))
info = client.get("/actuator/info").json()

print(info)
assert info.get("build", {}).get("commit") == app.BuildInfo.COMMIT, f"nothing contributed: {info}"
print("the deployed commit is one HTTP call away")

hints: The class has to implement the InfoContributor protocol.
Its method is contribute(), returning a dict that gets merged into the response.

levels.title: Metrics and hot refresh
levels.description:
The other two endpoints

  • /actuator/metrics serves the default prometheus_client registry - the meeting point with pico-otel, which writes into that same registry. Without the extra it answers 501 instead of pretending: pip install pico-actuator[metrics].
  • POST /actuator/refresh is the HTTP face of container.refresh_config(): change the configuration source, call it, and the response lists the prefixes that changed. Modules that follow live configuration - pico-resilience, pico-caching - pick the new values up with no restart.

A compose stack with Prometheus actually scraping this endpoint lives in pico-examples, asserted by a smoke test rather than described.
